title: Core concepts
description: Build durable, observable agents with bounded authority.

lessons.title: Architecture & durable execution
lessons.description: Build durable, observable agents with bounded authority.
lessons.conceptOverview: Use a fixed workflow when the steps are known. Routers select handlers; planner-executor and supervisor architectures allocate work dynamically. Long-running agents require durable state, checkpoints and explicit transitions. External side effects need idempotency keys or reconciliation because retries can repeat actions.

sections.title: Try it yourself
sections.content: Model a research assistant as a state machine. Crash immediately after a tool succeeds but before state is saved; design recovery without duplicating the action.

commonMistakes: Retrying every failed step is safe for external side effects.
keyTakeaways: Use a fixed workflow when the steps are known.

lessons.title: Computer use & memory
lessons.description: Build durable, observable agents with bounded authority.
lessons.conceptOverview: A computer-use agent observes an environment, chooses an action and verifies the resulting state. UI text is untrusted input. Episodic memory records events, semantic memory stores facts and procedural memory captures reusable methods. Retrieval and consolidation need provenance, expiration and correction policies.

sections.content: Design an observe-act-verify loop for a browser form. Define stale-state detection, action limits and which actions require explicit user authorization.

lessons.title: Trajectory evaluation
lessons.description: Build durable, observable agents with bounded authority.
lessons.conceptOverview: Task completion alone can hide unsafe or expensive trajectories. Measure tool selection and argument accuracy, policy violations, recovery rate, cost and latency. Evaluate repeat runs because stochastic agents can vary. Report failures by step and maintain adversarial cases alongside normal tasks.
